title: Elazar Ze’ira
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A great man in Shmuel’s time, as related in Bava Kamma 59b. Elazar Ze’ira was wearing black shoes (he went in black sandals) and standing in the market of Nehardea. The Exilarch’s men found him and asked him why he was going in black sandals; he answered that he was mourning for Jerusalem. They said to him: “Are you important enough to mourn for Jerusalem?” They thought it was arrogance; they brought him and imprisoned him. He said to them: “I am a great man.” They said to him: “How do we know?” He said to them: “Either you ask me something, or I will ask you something.” They said to him: “You ask.” He said to them: “One who cuts off unripe dates — what does he pay?” They could not answer him properly. They said to him: “Tell us.” He said: “Its value within sixty.” They said to him: “Who says as you do?” He said to them: “Shmuel is alive and the court exists.” They sent to Shmuel, who said to them: “He tells you well: within sixty,” and they released him.

notes.text: כופרא refers here to unripe dates, not necessarily cutting down the entire palm. בששים is the proportional assessment formula, retained without inventing a monetary figure.

The consulted account begins with the name Eliezer Zeira at the end of Bava Kamma 59a and continues on 59b. Hyman supplies Elazar. The black shoes, imprisonment, unripe dates, assessment within sixty, consultation with Shmuel and release are directly present; the names are not silently harmonized.
